segment_materiality.instructions: Judge only the SEGMENT UNDER REVIEW, reading the preceding turns for context. Does that segment contribute anything an equity analyst should record as a claim about the business? An answer that only makes sense beside the question before it is still material if the answer itself carries the content.

criteria.material: The segment carries something an equity analyst would record: any figure; any statement about guidance or outlook, however hedged; management explaining a reported result; a stated risk, watch area or caveat; management's own view of the business, its strategy, leadership or succession; or the substance of a question an analyst asked. A short segment is not immaterial by virtue of being short.
criteria.immaterial: The segment adds nothing an analyst would record. This covers operator logistics and dial-in instructions, thank-yous and 'next question please', closing pleasantries, the standard forward-looking-statements disclaimer, a repeated speaker banner, and short conversational fragments carrying no content of their own -- an interrupted half-sentence, or bare agreement such as 'Yeah, exactly' or 'I am saying the same thing'.

An answer that only makes sense beside the question before it is still material if the answer itself carries the content.

criteria.material: The segment carries something an equity analyst would record: any figure; any statement about guidance or outlook, however hedged; management explaining a reported result; a stated risk, watch area or caveat; management's own view of the business, its strategy, leadership or succession; or the substance of a question an analyst asked. A short segment is not immaterial by virtue of being short.
criteria.immaterial: The segment adds nothing an analyst would record. This covers operator logistics and dial-in instructions, thank-yous and 'next question please', closing pleasantries, the standard forward-looking-statements disclaimer, a repeated speaker banner, and short conversational fragments carrying no content of their own -- an interrupted half-sentence, or bare agreement such as 'Yeah, exactly' or 'I am saying the same thing'.

claim_record.claim_text: The firm increased its equity allocation to the CIB this quarter, moving roughly $150 million of NII from NII ex-Markets into Markets NII that is not expected to be offset in the bottom line.
claim_record.quote: you will have noted that we actually increased the equity allocation to the CIB this quarter for reasons that I think are pretty obvious in light of the amount of growth of supporting clients that we've done and the way that's playing through RWA. And so, that NII is moving out of NII ex. into Markets NII. And so, it's sort of a rare exception to the rule that changes in Markets NII are offset in the bottom line. caveats: Management said 'probably like $150 million'; this is a rough estimate.

claim_record.claim_text: A pre-event preview asserted that JPM's G-SIB capital requirement will be 5.2% by 2028 from 4.5%, calling it an approximately $20 billion hit to its capacity for buybacks and dividends.
claim_record.quote: The bank is disclosing in Q1 2026 that its new G-SIB (global systemically important bank) capital requirement will be 5.2% by 2028, from the existing 4.5%. That is an approximately $20B hit to JPM's ability to repurchase shares and pay dividends
caveats: This is a third-party preview's characterisation, not a figure JPM stated in this run's evidence; the 5.2%/4.5% surcharge figures are in a different sentence of the same page.

state_inputs.brief_passage: - **Third-party regulatory figures.** The preview's G-SIB requirement of 5.2% by 2028 is its own characterisation, not a figure JPM gave in this run's evidence [claim-133].
